_comment: The USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries publish several price series per commodity per
year. Picking one is a judgement, so the judgement lives here rather than in code.
Each entry is an ordered list of substrings matched against the USGS Statistics_detail
field; the first match wins, so a preferred series can be listed ahead of a fallback.
A mineral with no entry gets no USGS price and falls back to another source or the seed.
Match is case-insensitive.
copper: the LME grade A cash price is the international benchmark. The US producer
price includes a domestic premium and would overstate the value of trade that never
touches the United States.
cobalt: LME cash, for the same reason the US spot cathode price is not used.
lithium: battery-grade lithium carbonate. Flow volumes are carried on a contained-metal
basis expressed as lithium carbonate equivalent, so a carbonate price is the one that
matches the tonnage it multiplies.
rare-earths: NdPr oxide. This is the least comfortable choice on the list. There is no
published price for a mixed rare-earth oxide basket, and the two USGS series are a
cheap cerium-lanthanum mischmetal and an expensive NdPr oxide. NdPr is the series that
drives the economics of the magnet supply chain this app is about, but using it as a
basket proxy overstates the value of low-value rare-earth trade. Every value derived
from it is written to flows.json tagged source: estimated, and the interface labels it
as estimated wherever it appears.

copper: London Metal Exchange, grade A, cash
